rilua 0.1.27, vendored for atlantis4-script (Atlantis Evolution's Lua 5.1
scripts).

Origin: https://crates.io/api/v1/crates/rilua/0.1.27/download
SHA-256 of the .crate: 275971987852cab64d21d060e310b52982a7d9ffbac51acd654a1fd47ebad28b
Upstream: https://github.com/wowemulation-dev/rilua
Licence: MIT OR Apache-2.0 (LICENSE-MIT, LICENSE-APACHE), unchanged.

Kept from the package: Cargo.toml (as published), Cargo.toml.orig,
Cargo.lock, the licences, README.md, CHANGELOG.md, src/, tests/,
examples/, benches/. Left out: repository tooling (.github, .cargo,
.config, docs, scripts, rust-toolchain.toml and dot files).

The crate is excluded from the Native workspace (its dev-dependencies stay
out of Native's lock file). Its own test suite runs from this directory:
  cargo test --manifest-path vendor/rilua/Cargo.toml

Changes made in Native, each in its own commit with a reproducer test in
crates/atlantis4-script/tests/table_order.rs, so that tables iterate in
PUC-Rio Lua 5.1.4's order: see PATCHES below.

PATCHES

1. src/vm/table.rs, src/vm/execute.rs: `SETLIST` growing the array part
   rebuilds the hash part as PUC-Rio's `luaH_resizearray` does (it calls
   `resize`, which reinserts the hash nodes from last to first). rilua
   only extended the array, so constructors whose last item is a call
   (most nested layouts) iterated in another order.

2. src/vm/table.rs (`new_key`): a main position whose value is nil is
   taken by the new key, as in PUC-Rio's `newkey`. rilua reused it only
   once the old key's string had been collected, so a global set to nil
   and a later new global (ChangeWarp's callback resets) ended in another
   order.

3. src/vm/state.rs, src/stdlib/mod.rs, src/stdlib/package.rs: the
   globals table is created with `luaH_new(L, 0, 2)` and the libraries are
   opened in Lua 5.1.4's `linit.c` order, each registering its globals in
   PUC-Rio's order (`_G`, `base_funcs`, `_VERSION`, `ipairs`, `pairs`,
   `newproxy`; `package`, `module`, `require`); `package.loaded` receives
   the libraries opened after `package` at the end. A fresh `pairs(_G)`
   then walks in Lua 5.1.4's order.

4. src/vm/undump50.rs (new), src/lib.rs, src/vm/instructions.rs,
   src/vm/execute.rs, src/vm/debug_info.rs: Lua 5.0 binary chunks
   (Atlantis V's French DVD ships its scripts as Lua 5.0 bytecode).
   `compile_or_undump` sends a chunk whose header is `ESC "Lua" 0x50` to
   `undump50`, which re-encodes the 5.0 instructions in 5.1's layout
   (5.0's RK operands, constants reordered when an RK operand names a
   constant past 255) and gives the operations whose meaning differs
   their own codes, run as Lua 5.0.3's lvm.c runs them: ForLoop50,
   TForLoop50, TForPrep50 (generic `for` over a table), SetList50,
   SetListO50, NewTable50. Reproducer: crates/atlantis5-script/tests/
   lua50.rs (a chunk compiled by Lua 5.0.3's luac and the output of Lua
   5.0.3's lua). A corrupt chunk is a load error, never an abort or a
   panic: a vector's count past the bytes left fails before anything is
   reserved, and a size whose end wraps (an 8-byte size_t near 2^64)
   fails as truncated (Lua 5.0's lundump.c raises a memory or
   end-of-file error there, which the loaders catch). Reproducer: the
   tests of src/vm/undump50.rs (hand-made chunks, huge counts and sizes,
   every cut and byte change).

5. src/stdlib/coroutine.rs: `auxresume` made public, so an embedder can
   resume a coroutine from Rust (atlantis5-script runs each script as a
   coroutine that waits at the calls the original runs over frames).

6. src/vm/string.rs (`intern`): a string found in the table while it is
   dead (the other white, before the sweep frees it) gets the current
   white, as PUC-Rio's `luaS_newlstr` does. rilua returned it as it was,
   so the sweep freed a string a new constant or key had just taken
   (Atlantis V's scripts then failed with "attempt to concatenate a
   string value" under a busy collector). Reproducer: the walkthrough of
   crates/atlantis3-engine/tests/atlantis5_walkthrough.rs with
   A5_GC_STRESS set.

7. src/vm/table.rs, src/vm/state.rs: a table's `MAXBITS` per state.
   `Gc::table_max_bits` (26, Lua 5.1's) is given to every table
   `alloc_table` makes; a Lua 5.0.3 state sets 24, Lua 5.0.3's ltable.c
   value when `BITS_INT` > 26, so its hash part overflows at 2^24 nodes
   and keys past 2^24 are not counted for the array part. Atlantis V's
   chessboard asks `GetShortestPath(p, p)`, whose loop only ends on
   that `table overflow` (the 2^25th level); with 26 it grew past 6 GB.
   Reproducer: crates/atlantis3-engine/tests/atlantis5_puzzles.rs
   `chessboard_path_to_the_same_square_overflows` (run with --ignored).

8. src/vm/table.rs, src/vm/state.rs, src/bin/rilua.rs: Lua 5.0.3's table
   layout per state. `Gc::table_lua50` (false by default) is given to
   every table `alloc_table` makes; a table with it set runs Lua 5.0.3's
   ltable.c: `newkey` keeps `firstfree` on a node whose key is nil (from
   the last node down) and rehashes as soon as an insert takes the last
   one, the new key counted with the value `false` (5.1 grows when an
   insert finds no free node; an empty hash part is 5.0's one-node
   `dummynode`); `rehash` sizes the parts as 5.0's `numuse` and
   `computesizes` (`a >= 2^(i-1)`, the loop on `*narray >= 2^(i-1)`) and
   the hash part as 2^(floor(log2 n) + 1) nodes (n = 4 gives 8, 0 the
   dummy node); `resize` grows the array, makes the node vector,
   re-inserts a shrinking array's vanishing slice, then the old nodes
   from last to first. Lookups, `next`, `NewTable50` (log size C) and
   `SetList50` (plain `luaH_setnum` per item) already were 5.0's. Lua 5.1
   states keep the code above unchanged. atlantis5-script's `Script::new`
   sets it with `table_max_bits` 24, so `pairs` walks Atlantis V's tables
   (and its save writes the LUA_DB) in Lua 5.0.3's order. The `rilua`
   binary turns both on when its script is a Lua 5.0 binary chunk
   (header `ESC "Lua" 0x50`), for differential runs against Lua 5.0.3's
   `lua`. Not reproduced: a key whose value is nil and whose string the
   collector freed (5.0 then no longer finds the node, rilua may), which
   depends on each collector's timing. Reproducers: the `lua50_*` tests
   of src/vm/table.rs (orders printed by Lua 5.0.3's `lua`) and
   crates/atlantis5-script/tests/table_order.rs (the walk of `atl` after
   a new game and after events, the MD5 of Lua 5.0.3's walk).

9. src/vm/table.rs (`ensure_array_capacity`): on a table with Lua
   5.0.3's layout (patch 8), 5.1's `SETLIST` growing the array runs 5.0's
   `resize` at the current node count instead of 5.1's. 5.1's sets
   `last_free` one past the last node (its pre-decrement convention),
   which 5.0's `newkey` then read as a node index and panicked on. Only
   5.1 source compiled in a 5.0 state hits it (Native's own strings and
   test scripts); 5.0 chunks use `SetList50`, so the orders of patch 8
   are unchanged. Reproducer: the test
   `lua50_setlist_grows_the_array_of_a_table_with_hash_keys` of
   src/vm/table.rs and atlantis5-script's
   `a_constructor_with_hash_keys_and_a_call_builds`.

10. src/vm/gc/collector.rs (`over_alloc_limit`), src/vm/execute.rs: past
   the allocation limit (`set_alloc_limit`), a full collection runs
   before `LuaError::Memory` is raised, at each of the four checks
   (`gc_check`, `SETLIST`'s array growth, `table_set`, `vm_settable`).
   Before, the count stayed over the limit after the error until the
   incremental steps had swept the garbage, so every allocation after a
   memory error failed too, even once the run that made the garbage had
   ended; Lua 5.0's collector, a full one each time its threshold is met,
   frees it first. Only states with a limit set see a difference
   (atlantis5-script's, and testlib's `T.totalmem`). Reproducer:
   crates/atlantis3-engine/tests/atlantis5_puzzles.rs
   `chessboard_path_to_the_same_square_ends_on_a_memory_error` (the
   state's next global set failed with `not enough memory`).

11. src/compiler/codegen.rs, src/vm/state.rs, src/lib.rs, src/api.rs,
   src/stdlib/base.rs, src/stdlib/package.rs: Lua 5.0 source per state.
   `Gc::compile_lua50` (false by default) compiles the source loaded in
   the state with Lua 5.0.3's loops (lparser.c `forstat`, `fornum`,
   `forlist`, `forbody`): a numeric `for` whose variable is the loop's
   index (`SUB`, a jump, the body, `ForLoop50`: assigning the variable
   changes the iteration, closures in the loop share it), a generic `for`
   that starts with `TForPrep50` (a table as the iterator is walked with
   `next`) and whose first variable is the control value (`TForLoop50`),
   one breakable block for the body inside the variables' block. Lua 5.1
   states compile as before. Atlantis V's international DVD ships its
   scripts as Lua 5.0 source (the French DVD as 5.0 chunks of the same
   sources); 6 loops iterate a table directly and failed with "attempt
   to call a table value". atlantis5-script's `Script::new` sets it.
   Reproducers: crates/atlantis5-script/tests/lua50.rs
   `a_50_source_runs_as_lua_503_runs_it` (semantics.lua run as source
   prints what Lua 5.0.3's `lua` prints; as 5.1 source it fails) and
   crates/atlantis5-script/tests/international_dvd.rs (each of the 66
   scripts' 638 functions has the loop instructions, on the same lines,
   that Lua 5.0's `luac` put in the French DVD's chunks).
